content: Capsicum annuum is a domesticated species of the plant genus Capsicum, which is native to Mexico. The plant is an herbaceous annual with a densely branched stem. It typically grows to a height of 20 to 60 inches (approximately 0.5 meters). The plant produces single white flowers, which develop into fruits. These fruits are green when unripe and primarily turn red as they ripen, although some varieties may mature to shades of brown or purple. While Capsicum annuum can tolerate a wide range of climates, it thrives particularly well in warm and dry conditions. This adaptability, combined with the diversity of flavors it offers, has contributed to its rapid spread across the globe, potentially faster than any other crop originating from the New World. Capsicum annuum is widely cultivated for its use in food, producing both sweet peppers and hot chili peppers. Despite being a single species, it encompasses numerous cultivars with a variety of names. In American English, it is commonly referred to as chili pepper or bell pepper. In British English, all forms are generally called peppers. In Australian and Indian English, there is no universally used term for all its forms, but the term capsicum is often used specifically for bell peppers. Some common varieties of Capsicum annuum include: Aleppo Ancho Bell pepper Cubanelle Dundicut Jalapeño Pimento Poblano Tien Tsin In addition to its culinary uses, hot peppers derived from Capsicum annuum are also employed in medicine, particularly in Africa. John Lindley, a prominent botanist (1799–1865), documented its medicinal applications in his work Flora Medica (1838). He noted that Capsicum annuum was used in combination with Cinchona to treat intermittent and lethargic conditions, as well as atonic gout, dyspepsia accompanied by flatulence, tympanitis, and paralysis. Lindley further highlighted its significant value in the treatment of severe throat infections, such as cynanche maligna (a form of severe sore throat) and scarlatina maligna (a severe form of scarlet fever). In these cases, it was used either as a gargle or administered internally.
